_: The characters we do not type, and what they become.
This file is the single definition. It is committed identically in four repositories that
cannot import each other: this API, the management panel, and the two public websites. The
same arrangement as WebsiteCacheTags, and for the same reason. TypographyMapIsOneDefinitionTest
pins the Java map in Text/Typography.java against this file; each frontend's
scripts/check-typography.mjs reads its own copy.
'fold' is mechanical and reversible by eye: one character in, one string out. The spacing
comes from the text, not from the map, so ' · ' becomes ' | ' and 'a·b' becomes 'a|b' without
the map having to know which it is looking at.
'foldInternal' is the same, for box-drawing art that only ever appears in comments, log
banners and developer documentation. It is applied separately so a sweep of customer-facing
text never reshapes a diagram.
'manual' characters must not survive either, but their replacement depends on the sentence, so
the guard names them and a person decides. An arrow between two places becomes the word 'to';
the same arrow on a button is decoration and goes.
'keep' is the part that matters most. A clean-up that strips accents breaks five language
catalogues, a Spanish lodge's name and half the customer list.

manual.→: a route takes the word: 'Arusha to Serengeti'. On a button the arrow is decoration, so it goes.
manual.←: same: '< Back' reads as a glyph nobody typed. Drop it, or use an inline SVG chevron.
manual.↑: spell the direction, or use an icon
manual.↓: spell the direction, or use an icon
manual.↔: spell the direction, or use an icon
manual.⇒: 'becomes', 'leads to', or a plain '->' in developer notes
manual.★: a rating is an interface element, not a character: use the StarRating SVG component
manual.●: a tier meter is an interface element: use the TierDots SVG component
manual.✓: in a subject line it reads as clip-art. Say the thing: 'Backup completed'.
manual.⚠: say the thing. A warning sign in a subject line is not more urgent, only harder to search.
manual.²: '14,763 km²' becomes '14,763 sq km'. Rewording, not substitution.
manual.°: spell it, or keep it if it is a real coordinate. Eight occurrences, decide at the diff.

keepRules: Any letter carrying a diacritic, in any language. The de, es, fr, it and pt catalogues are built from them, and so are supplier names (Sueños Luxury Camp) and customer names. Folding these is the one mistake in this exercise that loses meaning rather than style.
Any character outside the Latin script. uk.json is roughly 25,000 Cyrillic characters, and the websites' Navbar lists language names natively: 日本語, 中文, 한국어, العربية, हिन्दी, Українська.
The non-breaking space before ! and ? in fr.json. That is correct French typography, not a stray character.

The three decode tables that must hold the real characters because they are what does the decoding: HtmlToText's entity map, PdfTemplateValidationService.HTML_ENTITIES, and the mask markers in TranslationService.
This file, the Java map that mirrors it, the guards that read it, and any test asserting on these characters.
Anything a customer, a visitor or a supplier wrote themselves: contact messages, booking inquiries, a guest's own testimony text, and received mail. Rewriting those falsifies a record.

_: Punctuation that belongs to a language, in the files that are written in it.
German writes „Anführungszeichen“, French writes « guillemets » and spells l’hôtel with a
curly apostrophe, and both put a non-breaking space before ! and ?. Those are not
typographic affectation, they are how the language is written, and folding them would
anglicise seven translations so that a German reader sees English quotation marks around
Spanish opens a question with ¿ and an exclamation with ¡; without them the sentence is
not punctuated, it is broken.
German words. It is the same judgement as keeping é: the character is carrying meaning.
Dashes and ellipses are not in this list, because no language requires them.
The English and Swahili catalogues are not in this list either, so they are folded in full.
